annotations.keyFindings: Travel and parking were 41 percent of out-of-pocket spending; rural patients spent twice as much on travel; spending peaked in the first six weeks.

synthesis: Six retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. A multicentre survey found moderate or severe financial toxicity in 38 percent of adults on systemic therapy, concentrated among younger, lower-income, not working and distant patients, probably underestimated by non-response. Travel and parking dominate out-of-pocket spending. A single distress-screening item misses about four in ten affected patients. Multi-mode, multilingual administration substantially reduces non-response bias. Financial toxicity is associated with poorer adherence, and a navigator service lowered spending without a comparison group.
gradeRationale: Consistent survey evidence with validated measures and a measurement study for the prevalence and screening questions; adherence and navigation evidence is weaker. Moderate certainty for prevalence and screening agreement.
summary: Six retrieved records appraised; five claims recorded; overall certainty moderate.
